title: 자요·차요·짜요: 예사소리·거센소리·된소리 한눈에
objective: You can tell plain, aspirated and tense consonants apart and say them correctly.
summary: A quick review of Korean plain, aspirated and tense consonants side by side.

task.title: Hear and choose the sound
task.line: Say each word out loud first, then choose or write the answer.

letters.sound: Light [k t p ch] at the start; [g d b j] between vowels
letters.as: Relaxed, a little air: 바다 sounds like [pada] (light p at the start, d between vowels).

letters.sound: [kʰ tʰ pʰ chʰ]: a strong puff of air
letters.as: Like k in 'kite' with extra breath; a tissue held in front of your mouth moves.

letters.sound: [kk tt pp jj]: tight throat, almost no air
letters.as: Like k in 'sky' or p in 'spy': short, tense, no puff.

exercises: Is the letter in brackets plain, aspirated, or tense? ① 바지 (ㅂ) ② 피자 (ㅍ) ③ 꼬리 (ㄲ)
Choose the word that matches the English: ① It's cheap. (사요 / 싸요) ② I'm sleeping. (자요 / 차요 / 짜요) ③ It hurts. (아파요 / 아빠요)
Choose the consonant that completes the word: ① card: _ㅏ드 (ㄱ / ㅋ / ㄲ) ② older brother: 오_ㅏ (ㅂ / ㅍ / ㅃ) ③ map: _ㅣ도 (ㅈ / ㅊ / ㅉ)
Choose the right word for the sentence: ① I take the bus. 버스 (타요 / 따요). ② This hat is big. 이 모자 (커요 / 꺼요). ③ Are you going again? (도 / 또) 가요?
answers: ① plain ② aspirated ③ tense
① 싸요 ② 자요 ③ 아파요
① ㅋ (카드) ② ㅃ (오빠) ③ ㅈ (지도)
① 타요 ② 커요 ③ 또
